title: installer: upgrade/rollback tooling - version pinning, backup/restore hooks, schema migrations, downgrade guards
author: Linh Nguyen
description:
Motivation: Private deployments require a predictable, reversible upgrade path. Customers reported failed upgrades when operator-managed state (Postgres, object storage pointers, and configmaps) changed shape. This PR adds explicit version pinning, a pre-upgrade backup hook, idempotent schema migrations, and downgrade-guards to prevent accidental data loss during rollback.

What this PR does:
- Adds Chart and Terraform-level version pinning to guarantee compatible asset sets during upgrades.
- Introduces a Helm pre-upgrade Job that performs consistent backups of Postgres (pg_dump), uploads to configured object storage, and records a backup manifest in a k8s Secret.
- Adds a post-upgrade verification Job that checks service health, schema versions, and verifies the backup manifest matches the running state.
- Implements an idempotent migration runner (migrate.sh + migration manifest) which records applied migrations and is safe to re-run.
- Adds a downgrade-guard controller that prevents Helm rollbacks when irreversible migrations are recorded; guard can be bypassed with explicit operator approval via a k8s annotation.
- Adds Terraform module changes to pin provider and module versions and a migration helper for infra state changes.
- Adds an UPGRADE_RUNBOOK.md with step-by-step instructions, and CI e2e tests that validate the happy-path upgrade and a simulated failed upgrade + restore.

Checklist (high level):
- [x] Chart version pinning and values schema change
- [x] Pre-upgrade backup Job and manifest Secret
- [x] Idempotent migration runner and migration history table
- [x] Downgrade guard with explicit bypass annotation and audit event
- [x] Terraform module version pinning and helper script
- [x] Runbook and docs
- [x] CI integration tests added

Testing performed:
- Local kind cluster: performed upgrade from v1.18.0 -> v1.19.0 with sample data; confirmed backup manifest and restore succeed.
- Integration pipeline: ran upgrade e2e which performed pre-backup, migration, post-verify, and smoke tests (integration-upgrade job).
- Simulated failed migration: aborted post-verify and exercised restore path (pg restore + reconcile), verified services reached steady-state.

Rollback/restore plan (docs summary):
1) If post-upgrade verification fails, the restore job reads the latest backup manifest Secret and restores Postgres and object storage pointers.
2) The downgrade-guard prevents a normal Helm rollback if irreversible migrations exist; operator must add annotation "redwood.io/force-rollback: yes" and run the guarded rollback runbook which includes manual migration compensation steps.

Compatibility notes:
- Migration runner uses a versioned migration table (redwood_schema_migrations) so older operators can safely detect applied migration ids.
- Helm charts retain backward-compatible value names; when breaking renames are required, mapping code is added to values schema to smooth transitions.

Rollout plan:
- Stage in Canary cluster with golden dataset and run integration-upgrade pipeline.
- Promote to staging; run scheduled nightly upgrade test.
- Enable in customer-private clusters by default in the next minor release; operators can opt-in until GA.

Security & compliance: backups are uploaded to configured customer object storage; default retention is 30 days, configurable via values. Backup manifests are stored in k8s Secrets with RBAC restricted to the installer service account.

References: Linear ENG-2145 (upgrade tooling), ENG-2209 (downgrade guards), SUP-701 (customer incident that motivated this work).
